scope: Nine primary texts; limited related query search; not exhaustive priority adjudication

papers.title: Better product formulas for quantum phase estimation
papers.assumptions: Gapped eigenstate and analytic effective Hamiltonian; low-energy specialization assumes PSD fast-forwardable groups, bounded locality/degree and O(1) groups/exponentials.
papers.guarantee_target: Eigenvalue perturbation coefficients; specialized low-energy bounds and custom two-group formulas.
papers.cost_information: Step and precision scaling; does not make arbitrary molecular expectation values or fast-forwarding free.
papers.relation: Energy-specific PF and low-energy analysis are prior art; not an independently established nonlocal PF-native SOS construction.
papers.limitations: Read relevant main sections, not all supplement proofs.

papers.title: Better bounds for low-energy product formulas
papers.assumptions: k-local commuting groups, interaction norm J, degree d; stronger cost claims use PSD groups and fixed group count. Fermionic extension retains mode-degree dependence.
papers.cost_information: Trotter number rather than a compiled controlled molecular ground-energy task cost.
papers.relation: Restricted-commutator proof architecture is known; density factorization alone does not supply the favorable locality constants.
papers.limitations: Relevant sections and leakage assumptions checked, not every supplemental derivation.

papers.title: Trotterization is substantially efficient for low-energy states
checked_sections: Supplement S2: Theorem S1 Eq.S5; PDF printed page 8
Proof mechanism: Eq.S12; Corollary S2 Eq.S23 located
papers.assumptions: PSD k-local terms; g-extensiveness; commuting layers. Favorable asymptotic statements use fixed k and account for layer count and low-energy leakage.
papers.guarantee_target: Finite low-energy evolution error; projected nested-commutator bound linear in energy.
papers.cost_information: Trotter number with locality/extensiveness parameters; molecular dense fragments need their actual parameters.
papers.relation: Linear low-energy dependence is explicit prior art. A global-support specialization loses favorable size scaling; not evidence of a novel generic gap-proportional coefficient theorem.
papers.limitations: Browser HTML body displayed 2026-08-24, differing from v1 PDF. PDF main setup and Supplement S2 theorem were rechecked; no local PDF-byte SHA attestation. Full supplement not independently reproved.

papers.title: Spectral analysis of product formulas for quantum simulation
checked_sections: Comparison between first and second order product formulas: Eq.21 and two-layer similarity
Application in quantum phase estimation: Theorem 2 Eqs.23-27
papers.assumptions: Isolated target spectral branch with appropriate effective-Hamiltonian gap conditions.
papers.guarantee_target: Eigenvalue error and eigenstate-overlap effects in QPE/RPE.
papers.cost_information: Precision/step/gap dependence; success probability depends on overlap.
papers.relation: Spectral/task-specific PF analysis is known; does not itself construct chemistry SOS fragments.
papers.limitations: Publisher version identified by DOI; webpage was read, supplementary notes not fully audited.

papers.title: Fast quantum simulation of electronic structure by spectrum amplification
papers.published_title: Fast Quantum Simulation of Electronic Structure by Spectral Amplification
checked_sections: III: Eqs.13-23, Gram SDP and generating algebra
papers.assumptions: SOS generators and corresponding block-encoding access; approximate chemistry factorizations must track Hamiltonian error.
papers.guarantee_target: Spectral-amplification ground-energy estimation rather than a native PF eigenvalue-bias certificate.
papers.cost_information: SOS gap competes with block-encoding normalization and preparation/lookup costs.
papers.relation: Chemistry SOS, Gram SDP, and DFTHC are prior constructions. Their resource multipliers are not transferable to this task.
papers.limitations: Relevant construction sections read; full resource tables and all appendices not audited or numerically reproduced.

papers.title: Quantum simulation with sum-of-squares spectral amplification
papers.version: arXiv:2505.01528v1 (2025); distinct from later journal version
checked_sections: Theorems 4,5,7: statements/access conditions; Theorem 4 starting proof
papers.assumptions: Block encoding, controlled queries/inverses, and state or state-preparation access as specified for each task.
papers.cost_information: Low-energy scale, normalization, overlap and information availability affect query/gate complexity.
papers.relation: PSD shifts and near-frustration-free low-energy advantage are known; not a native PF finite-step theorem.

papers.title: Near-frustration-free electronic structure Hamiltonian representations and lower bound certificates
checked_sections: II.1: Eqs.2-6 weighted SOS and equality constraints
III.3: Eqs.63-80 spin-free algebra and particle-number ideal
IV ending: primal/dual conversion limitations; V setup read only
papers.assumptions: Specified truncated fermionic algebra, PSD Gram, normal-order coefficient matching, symmetry constraints.
papers.guarantee_target: SOS lower-bound representations and relation to v2RDM/weighted dual certificates.
papers.cost_information: SDP size follows generating algebra; converting to a PF-native Hermitian square class may alter rank and lower bound.

papers.limitations: No numerical table reuse, solver execution, or universal PF-native closure inferred.

papers.title: Theory and practice of Trotter product formulas for quantum chemistry
checked_sections: III.1-3: PF, near-integrability and processing (relevant text)
V.2-3: per-step cost versus Trotter/leakage error; leading-bias methodology
papers.assumptions: Specific factorization/fast-forwardable fragments and task-defined error/cost model; leakage for enlarged representations.
papers.guarantee_target: SPRINT/GRADE construction and empirical resource analysis of chemistry evolution/spectroscopy.
papers.cost_information: Per-step Givens/diagonal-phase implementation and number of steps must be combined.
papers.relation: Strong PF/circuit-cost baselines; leading-error estimation is not a strict finite-step SOS certificate.
papers.limitations: Relevant construction/resource methodology checked; complete proofs and gate tables not independently reproduced.

papers.title: Quantum matrix arithmetics with Hamiltonian evolution
checked_sections: 6.3: Hermitian one-body squares and fixed-particle seminorm Eqs.263-264; following proof setup
papers.assumptions: Hamiltonian block-encoding input operations and controls; Hamiltonian QSVT/squaring constructions; particle-preserving terms for sector seminorms.
papers.guarantee_target: SOS time-evolution implementation with commutator-dependent cost.
papers.cost_information: Additional ancilla and subroutine query costs; direct orbital-rotation square exponentials use a different access model.
papers.relation: Close prior art explicitly combining SOS, PF and chemistry squares; broad SOS-plus-PF novelty claim is untenable. Does not by itself establish equivalence to the audited SOS-gap ground-eigenvalue certificate.
papers.limitations: Relevant sections read in v1 and checked against v3; full QSVT proofs and higher-order complexity analysis not reproduced. No algorithm from this paper was implemented.
